newsitem.title: UK: UK inflationary pressures build in Q4 - survey.
newsitem.headline: UK inflationary pressures build in Q4 - survey.

text.p: The British economy performed strongly in the last quarter of 1996, but there were some signs of a modest build up of inflationary pressures, a leading business group said on Monday.

The Institute of Directors (IoD) said in its December survey of business opinion that both prices and costs in the UK were increasing faster, although the overall picture was still one of modest acceleration.
"The economy is performing strongly and jobs are being created," said Ruth Lea, Head of the IoD's Policy Unit.

"But with inflationary pressures building up...I would recommend, and I expect on balance, a small increase in base rates after this week's meeting between the Chancellor and the Governor of the Bank of England."
The two are due to meet on Wednesday.
The survey said the average level of pay awards in December was not significantly different from September's, but at 4.6 percent was still well ahead of inflation.

It said 75 percent of directors said their companies performed well in the fourth quarter, little changed from the previous quarter. In addition, nine percent of respondents reported full capacity compared with only four percent in the third quarter. The IoD said manufacturing was the best performing sector in the last three months of 1996, with exports still buoyant despite the strength of the pound, and employment growth was still positive.
"Moreover, with the majority of directors optimistic about their prospects for the forthcoming quarter, the outlook looks positive for 1997," it said.
Small firms created significantly more jobs than medium-sized and large companies in the last quarter of 1996, despite evidence the latter performed better.
